fix.summary:
Two of the four are now closed at the request path and proven by driving it; two are partial for reasons that live entirely outside my ownership, and I am naming those loudly rather than papering over them.

performance-11 is FIXED and is the one that was pure "machinery never mounted". The tenant home page now makes ONE call to the mounted `/t/:slug/summary` and `safeCount` is deleted. Proven by booting the real Next app and the real API and server-rendering `/el/t/<slug>` twice — once with HEAD's page.tsx, once with mine — against a seeded 5,006-title library. HEAD: five list calls, tiles render `1 · 1 · 100 · 100 · 100`. Mine: one `GET /t/:slug/summary`, tiles render `5006 · 800 · 400 · 150 · 250`. I also fixed the latent cache bug the refutation flagged (`books > 0 && members > 0` never cached a library with a catalogue and no members yet; now `||`).

performance-05 is closed for the SHIPPED posture and halved for the enforced one. The refutation's exact gap — no `isUnlimitedInt` short-circuit in quota.interceptor.ts — is closed, and I additionally removed `@RequiresQuota('max_books')` from BooksController because BooksService.create already enforces the same 402 race-safely inside the insert's transaction, so the decorator was buying a second full catalogue scan. Proven with Postgres statement logging around a real POST: shipped posture 1 → 0 executions of `SELECT COUNT(*) … FROM "public"."books" WHERE "archivedAt" IS NULL`; enforced posture 2 → 1; and the route still answers 402 at a finite ceiling with the book count unmoved. What is NOT closed: under BILLING_ENABLED=true the surviving in-transaction count is still a 13,333-buffer seq scan (needs a tenant migration I do not own), and members' identical lock+count is untouched (members.service.ts, not mine).

performance-12: I closed the third catalogue table — authors — which was unguarded in a file I DO own and which the previous round missed. Members and collection records remain untouched because they are outside my ownership. I must flag loudly that the previous round shipped a user-facing regression that my authors change adds one more surface to: Combobox defaults `minQueryChars = 1`, so book/author pickers send 1–2 character queries the API now answers empty, with no hint. I added the bilingual `search.minChars` string so that fix is a one-liner, but the fix itself is in files I do not own.

performance-07: no diff, deliberately. The verifier itself said the refusal was a scoping verdict, not a defect verdict, and I independently re-confirmed the blocker: Privacy Policy §6 still reads `[30]`, `[14]`, `[up to 5–10]`, `[a limited period, e.g. 90 days]`, and grepping the control schema finds exactly one stated period (the 30-day Stripe payload line) — which is already enforced. Inventing four deletion schedules would be a worse failure than leaving it open, so this is blocked-on-owner with the exact numbers and the exact limbs they unblock.

Suites: 766/766 unit, 205/205 integration (28 files), `pnpm check:translations` green, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in apps/api and apps/web. Every new test was verified to FAIL against the reintroduced bug before being kept.

Environment left as found: billing.enabled row and max_books override deleted, per-database log_statement reset, scratch index rolled back, ports 4598/4599 clear. Note `apps/web/AGENTS.md` and `apps/web/CLAUDE.md` are untracked artifacts that `next dev` writes when it runs — my SSR probe created them; they are not part of my change.

One thing I checked so a verifier does not have to: `apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/onboarding/page.tsx:75-76` also reads `items.length` off `limit=1` calls, but only as a `count > 0` boolean for step-completion flags. findings_addressed.why_the_last_attempt_failed: The gate was put in BooksService.create and proved with a unit test that constructs the service by hand — a path the HTTP request never takes first. Over HTTP, BooksController is @UseInterceptors(QuotaInterceptor) with @RequiresQuota('max_books'), and quota.interceptor.ts resolved `limit` and then called countUsage() unconditionally, with no isUnlimitedInt check anywhere in the file. So in the configuration the product actually ships (BILLING_ENABLED=false, where unlimitedPlan() rewrites every int feature to UNLIMITED_INT) a book create still ran the identical full catalogue scan; what the change removed was the advisory lock and the service's own second scan, not the scan. The unit test could not see it because it never touches the interceptor. On top of that, two of the three shapes the finding names by line number — members create and members un-archive — were byte-for-byte unchanged, and the partial index the finite-ceiling path depends on was never added.
findings_addressed.what_changed: apps/api/src/plans/quota.interceptor.ts:88 now short-circuits with `if (isUnlimitedInt(limit)) return next.handle();` BEFORE resolving a tenant client or calling countUsage. This is generic, so it also stops the max_members and staff_seats counters running in the shipped posture. The QUOTA_COUNTERS registration check stays ahead of it so a typo'd feature key still 500s instead of silently becoming 'no quota' (covered by a new unit test). Separately, apps/api/src/catalog/books.controller.ts drops @RequiresQuota('max_books') from create: BooksService.create already runs the count and the insert inside one transaction behind pg_advisory_xact_lock('quota:<tenant>:max_books:'), throwing the same structured 402, so the interceptor's pre-check was the racy duplicate of a check that already runs — and it cost a second full catalogue scan. @UseInterceptors stays mounted at class level (documented) so a future @RequiresQuota route here cannot silently no-op. Tests: 3 new unit tests in quota.interceptor.spec.ts (verified to fail 2/2 with the guard removed) and 2 new integration tests driving POST /t/:slug/catalog/books through the real AppModule — one counting book.count calls on the app's own cached Prisma client during a real request (verified: reads 1 with the bug reintroduced, 0 with the fix), one arming subscriptions + a finite max_books override and asserting the route still answers 402 with the book count unmoved. afterAll disarms the global switch unconditionally so no sibling spec inherits it.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: OUT OF MY OWNERSHIP, AND THE FINDING STAYS OPEN FOR IT. (1) With BILLING_ENABLED=true the surviving in-transaction count is still `Seq Scan on books, Buffers: shared read=13333, Execution Time: 67.7 ms` at 400k titles. I proved the fix: creating `CREATE INDEX books_active_idx ON books (id) WHERE "archivedAt" IS NULL` inside a rolled-back transaction on perf_scale turns it into `Index Only Scan using books_active_idx, Buffers: shared hit=1 read=1527, 28.7 ms` — 8.7x fewer buffers. That is a tenant migration under packages/db-tenant/prisma/migrations/ which I do not own. It is also 13,333 of the dashboard summary's 17,107 buffers, so the same one index closes the cost half of performance-11. (2) apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:318 and :451 still take the advisory lock and count; MembersController still carries @RequiresQuota('max_members'), so under the enforced posture a member create still counts twice. Measured: `Seq Scan on members, Buffers: shared hit=2222, 11.9 ms` at 100,000 members. The same two-line change applies (drop the decorator, since members.service already enforces transactionally) plus `CREATE INDEX members_active_idx ON members (id) WHERE "archivedAt" IS NULL AND status <> 'archived'`.

findings_addressed.why_the_last_attempt_failed: Textbook machinery-built-and-never-mounted. GET /t/:slug/summary was built, mounted, integration-tested and correct — and had ZERO callers anywhere in apps/web. The finding's own `where` is apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/page.tsx and that file had an empty diff, so the product still defined safeCount returning res.items.length and still fired five list endpoints per server render, with books and members asked at limit=1 so a 400,000-title catalogue rendered its tile as '1'. The report was honest that it was partial; the defect reproduced unchanged in the product. The refutation also flagged a latent bug for when it WAS wired: dashboard.service.ts cached only when `books > 0 && members > 0`, so a library with a catalogue and no members yet would recompute the whole statement on every render.
findings_addressed.what_changed: apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/page.tsx: safeCount is DELETED and the five list calls with it; one safeSummary() call to `/t/${slug}/summary` feeds all five tiles. The API-down path still degrades to '—' tiles rather than blanking the page, and because `summary` is null on that path the onboarding welcome (keyed on zero-books-AND-zero-members) is no longer shown to a library whose API merely failed to answer — which the old null-count arithmetic got right by accident and which I made explicit. apps/api/src/dashboard/dashboard.service.ts:127 changes `&&` to `||`, so only the literal brand-new-library state stays uncached; the onboarding nudge may be up to 30 s stale, which is acceptable for a banner suggesting a next step. Two new integration tests: one archives every member, proves the summary reports members=0 with books>0 and that the SECOND read is served from cache (the exact case the old guard never cached), restoring in a finally; one reads the page file with comments stripped and asserts it fetches /summary and contains no `items.length`, no `safeCount` and none of the five list URLs — a wiring guard that fails against HEAD, which is the only property that makes it worth having.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: The summary statement uncached is 17,107 shared buffers versus roughly 4,400 for the five list calls it replaces, so the 30 s Redis cache is load-bearing rather than a nicety: below about four renders per 30 s window this is a cost regression, above it a win, and correctness is a win at every rate. books_active_idx (see performance-05) removes 13,333 of those 17,107 and makes it unconditional. I corrected the finding's cost claim in the code comment: 'two full scans of loans at 32,845 buffers each' is STALE — performance-02's indexes landed, and re-measured on the 400k fixture those calls are now Index Scan using loans_status_loanedAt_id_idx (52 buffers), Index Only Scan using loans_status_dueAt_id_idx (6) and Index Scan using books_sortTitle_idx (11). What this actually removes is five HTTP round trips and ~15 statements per render, plus five wrong numbers.

Its `what` names members_search_trgm beside books_search_trgm, its `impact` says 'on the members screen it costs 100,000 rows', and its `fix` says to enforce the floor 'for books, members AND collection records'. members.service.ts:199 and collection-records.service.ts:57 were byte-for-byte unchanged, both still doing `{ contains: normalizeText(opts.q) }`, and both already import from '../catalog/normalize.js' so it was not a dependency problem. The attempt also SHIPPED a regression: apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx defaults minQueryChars = 1, so the checkout and hold book pickers now send one- and two-character queries that the API answers with an empty page, producing a silently blank dropdown with no 'keep typing' hint, where matches used to appear.
findings_addressed.what_changed: apps/api/src/catalog/authors.service.ts now runs the same classifySearchTerm floor as BooksService.list and returns `{ items: [], nextCursor: null, minQueryChars: 3 }` for a shorter term. Authors is the THIRD table in apps/api/src/catalog with the identical shape — `sortName LIKE '%q%'` against authors_sortname_trgm, reachable from the same URL-driven DataTable search box and from AuthorPicker — and the previous round missed it. Proven over the real HTTP route: q=ομ returns 0 items with minQueryChars=3 and Postgres executes ZERO statements against authors, while ομη / Ομή / ΟΜΗΡ each return the Greek author, so the floor is length and not the term. Three new integration tests assert exactly that. I also added the bilingual hint string `search.minChars` to locales/el and locales/en (Greek first, check:translations green) so the web-side fix below is a one-liner rather than a translation exercise. I was deliberately honest in the comment about size: at the audit's 20,000-author fixture a two-character term is `Seq Scan on authors, Buffers: shared hit=246, 1.88 ms` and a three-character term ALSO seq-scans, so the win here is 'the query is not run at all', not 'the index takes over' — the 1,915x crossover the finding measured is the catalogue's.
findings_addressed.residual_risk: TWO THINGS ARE STILL OPEN AND BOTH ARE OUTSIDE MY OWNERSHIP. (1) The members and collection-record halves of the conjunction. I re-measured the members half myself: `Seq Scan on members … Rows Removed by Filter: 100000, Buffers: shared hit=3 read=2222, 18.5 ms` for a two-character term, with no rate limit anywhere near the route. The change is three lines in each of apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:199 and apps/api/src/customization/collection-records.service.ts:57, copying what authors.service.ts now does. (2) THE SHIPPED UX REGRESSION, WHICH MY AUTHORS CHANGE ADDS A THIRD SURFACE TO. Until apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx line 57 changes `minQueryChars = 1` to `minQueryChars = 3` and renders t('common.search.minChars', { count }) in place of combobox.noMatches, one- and two-character input at the checkout desk (loans/new/CheckoutForm.tsx), the hold desk (reservations/new/PlaceHoldForm.tsx) and now the author picker (components/AuthorPicker.tsx) yields an unexplained empty dropdown. apps/web/components/DataTable.tsx has no minQueryChars at all, so the catalogue and members search boxes have the same silent-empty problem. If the owner would rather not ship that UX until the web fix lands, reverting my authors change is one hunk — but the books half of the regression is already in the tree and must be fixed regardless.

findings_addressed.why_the_last_attempt_failed: Not a defect verdict — a scoping one, and the verifier said so explicitly. Everything that was built is correct and genuinely wired: the limb hangs off the already-registered 'retention-sweep' job, the migration re-applies cleanly and survives pg_dump/pg_restore, the prune is batched and self-emptying, and the integration test drives the real sweepRetention entry point. The finding, though, is 'SIX append-only tables have no retention sweep', and five still have none: control-plane audit_log, email_outbox (the worst growth rate in the whole finding — one full-body row per overdue loan per day into the SHARED control DB), announcement_deliveries, support_redemption_attempts/support_sessions, and stripe_webhook_events ROWS (the sweep blanks the body but never deletes the row). The reason four of those five were left is that nobody has published a period for them, and the previous agent refused to invent one.
findings_addressed.what_changed: NOTHING, deliberately, and I want that to be the visible answer rather than churn dressed up as progress. I re-verified the blocker myself instead of taking it on trust: locales/en/legal/privacy.md §6 lines 75/77/80/81 still read `[30]` days, `[14]`-day backups, `[up to 5–10]` years and `[a limited period, e.g. 90 days]`; and grepping packages/db-control/prisma/schema.prisma for a stated period finds exactly one — the 30-day line on StripeWebhookEvent.payloadJson at :721 — which is the one already enforced. Picking four numbers here would put a deletion schedule for patron personal data into production that no document promises and no counsel has seen, which is a worse failure than the unbounded growth. I re-ran the existing performance-07 tests as part of the suite and they pass (4/4).
findings_addressed.residual_risk: Unbounded growth on a shared volume persists for five tables. Two CORRECTIONS to the finding, from my own reading, so whoever picks this up scopes it right: announcement_deliveries holds only ids and four timestamps and CASCADEs from announcement, tenant AND user, so it is bounded by announcements x users rather than unbounded; and stripe_webhook_events rows are ~100 bytes with a real money-safety reason to keep them (processedAt is the durable guard against an operator's >30-day 'Resend' from the Stripe Dashboard replaying a stale subscription payload), so 'row count grows forever' is the right trade, not a bug. The genuinely open ones are control-plane audit_log and email_outbox. ONE DESIGN CONSTRAINT for the email_outbox limb, which is easy to get wrong: EmailOutbox.idempotencyKey is @unique and IS the dedup ledger (schema.prisma:770), so deleting sent rows re-arms duplicate sends — the limb must blank bodyMarkdown the way pruneStripeWebhookPayloads blanks payloadJson, keep the envelope row, and skip pending/sending rows. It must also not blank a body that is still an operator's only copy of a live one-time link: with EMAIL_DRIVER=console, AdminOutboxService is the ONLY path by which a librarian gets a verification or reset link, so the window must comfortably exceed those token TTLs.

Arming also writes a new Redis key `login:lock-scope:<uid>` holding the IP that armed it, with the same TTL. login() gates the durable lock through durableLockApplies(): marker present -> bar only the IP it names, everyone else falls through to the ordinary per-(account+IP) check; marker absent or Redis unreadable -> bar the account. Success clears the marker alongside the two existing keys. recordDegradedFailure was removed — the durable write now happens on every path, so the Redis-outage branch is just loud logging. writeLockScope refuses to scope on an unverified IP and logs at error, failing toward account-wide (stricter, never weaker). findings_addressed.what_changed:
TWO changes, both mounted and both proven by mutation.

(1) THE WRITE IS REFUSED. New `PlanPriceWriteInterceptor` (apps/api/src/billing/plan-price-write.interceptor.ts), registered as `{provide: APP_INTERCEPTOR, useClass: PlanPriceWriteInterceptor}` in billing.module.ts. It fires only when `context.getClass() === AdminPlansController && req.method === 'PATCH'`, and does zero DB/network work unless the body carries a price id or an amount/currency an already-stored id must keep matching. It refuses: a non-Price id (`prod_…`, empty string, copy-paste whitespace); a `price_seed_*` placeholder; the same id in both columns (Postgres accepts that — both unique indexes are satisfied); an id already backing another plan (previously a P2002 500); a Price Stripe has never heard of, an archived one, a currency mismatch, an integer minor-unit amount mismatch, and an interval/interval_count that does not match the column — the €39-a-month-billed-as-390-a-year case; an amount or currency edit that would desync an already-configured Price; and any price-id write on a host where the driver is not `real`, because an id this server cannot check is an id it cannot charge with.

WHY AN INTERCEPTOR AND NOT THE HANDLER: `apps/api/src/admin/admin-plans.controller.ts` is outside my ownership AND `BillingModule` already imports `AdminModule`, so having the plans controller inject a billing validator would close a module cycle. `APP_INTERCEPTOR` from a feature module is the supported Nest mechanism (same shape as `SupportAuditInterceptor` in app.module.ts). Deliberately NOT a guard: Nest runs global guards BEFORE controller guards, so a guard would have handed an unauthenticated caller a validator that makes outbound Stripe calls. Interceptors run after all guards — asserted: an anonymous PATCH returns 401, never 400.

(2) THE REPORT IS READ AUTOMATICALLY. `/admin/plans` and `/admin/plans/:slug` now call the catalogue endpoint on every visit and render the verdict — a per-plan 'reconciled / N problems' column and the problem text in full.
